white-hover.displayName: Pure White (hover state only: nav, index rows, [ Visit ])

display.purpose: The one word each stage owns. Hero: the name, always two lines. Build: `Build.`, one line.

display-mobile.purpose: The display role at 720px and below; the Hero name and the Build word both step to it. Second stop of the display ramp, not a separate voice.

body.purpose: Reserved reading voice, loaded on <body> at weights 400/500. No size, leading or measure set on any surface yet.

descriptor.purpose: The one mono sentence beside the stage word: Hero descriptor above the name, Build pitch under the print. Sentence case, mute. Measure 54ch in both stages.

index.purpose: Project names in the Build index (mute, ink when active) and the role title of each Ship frame (ink, weight 400). Sentence case; Build names bracketed on mobile.

label.purpose: Bracketed controls: navigation, the DZ mark, and the [ Visit host ] link. The only uppercase role.

data.purpose: Data and measurements: the scope column of the Build index, the Ship year labels, and the organisation and dates in each Ship frame. Sentence case, tabular numerals. Build scope and year labels hidden on mobile; frame dates stay.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing. Used by the develop/settle load animation and the 200ms hover colour step.

motion.name: develop
motion.value: 1.6s var(--ease-out) both; from { filter: brightness(0.05) contrast(1.6) } to { filter: brightness(1) contrast(1) }
motion.purpose: The photograph rises once from near-black to its true tones on load. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: 1.6s var(--ease-out) both; from { transform: translateY(24px) } to { transform: none }
motion.purpose: The copy block (descriptor + name) settles up 24px into place alongside develop. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: hover-step
motion.purpose: Text controls (nav links, index rows, [ Visit ]) step from mute to pure white. Transition removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: develop-on-change
motion.value: same keyframes as develop, applied to the active print in the Build window whenever the active project changes
motion.purpose: Every print change on a stage rises from near-black exactly like the Hero's load moment. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis ({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true }) driven by gsap.ticker; lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); lagSmoothing(0); index/anchor jumps scrollTo(y, { duration: 0.9 })
motion.purpose: One clock for scroll smoothing and scrubbing. Not created under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: stage-pin
motion.value: ScrollTrigger { start: 'top top', end: '+=' + innerHeight * steps, pin: true, scrub: true, anticipatePin: 1 }; active step = floor(progress * steps)
motion.purpose: A stage with several steps stays one pinned viewport and is scrubbed by scroll. Desktop (min-width 721px) and no-preference only.

motion.name: hero-exit
motion.value: gsap.to(photo, { yPercent: -8, filter: 'brightness(0.08)', ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { start: 'top top', end: 'bottom top', scrub: true } })
motion.purpose: As the Hero unpins its print sinks toward the ground and eases up 8% while the next word rises. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: strip-scrub
motion.value: gsap.to(track, { x: () => -(track.scrollWidth - (innerWidth - 2*gutter)), ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { start: 'top top', end: () => '+=' + distance*1.2, pin: true, scrub: true, anticipatePin: 1, invalidateOnRefresh: true } })
motion.purpose: Second pin grammar (Ship): the pinned stage drags a horizontal strip right-to-left by the scroll until its last label lands on the right gutter. Desktop (min-width 721px) and no-preference only.

motion.name: axis-draw
motion.value: gsap.from(axis, { scaleX: 0, transformOrigin: 'left center', duration: 1.2, ease: CustomEase.create('davidzo-out', '0.16,1,0.3,1'), scrollTrigger: { start: 'top 70%', once: true } })
motion.purpose: The Ship timeline axis draws once from the left on first entry and never again. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Uses the system's --ease-out bezier (0.16,1,0.3,1) registered as a GSAP CustomEase, so CSS and GSAP share one curve.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: portrait band crop, nav collapses to DZ + [ Talk ], scroll cue hidden; Build unpinned, height auto, single column, 2x2 bracketed index, 4:3 print window. Ship unpinned, height auto, axis/ticks/years hidden, frames become hairline-separated rows beside a vertical hairline.

breakpoints.name: pin
breakpoints.purpose: min-width (with prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference): stages pin and scrub, by steps (Build) or by distance (Ship).

grain.implementation: Generated <canvas> white-noise greyscale field, regenerated on resize via ResizeObserver, static otherwise. Every stage mounts its own.
grain.zIndex: 2 (Hero, above photo and veil) / 1 (Build, above the print; Ship, above the ground, under the transparent frames); always below text
grain.note: Direction contract said ~10%; the build ships 0.14. Build wins.

photograph.grading: Left field and frame edges burned to #0b0b0b in the asset; no CSS vignette on desktop.
photograph.mobile: 66svh band, object-position: 78% 0, CSS veil linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(11,11,11,0) 55%, rgba(11,11,11,1) 100%)

prints.source: Screenshot of the product's own public landing at 1000x900 (headless Chromium), 2026-09-13.
prints.grading: Greyscale, contrast 1.06, brightness 0.96, blacks lifted to #0b0b0b, edges burned toward #0b0b0b with per-landing strength (dark landings left 0.8 / right 0.7 / top 0.5 / bottom 0.6 over 10% / 6% / 5% / 8%; Sincerin no top burn because its nav bar is white; Strickle, light, 0.28 / 0.22 / 0 / 0.3). JPEG q0.86.
prints.provenance: Recipe embedded in each JPEG COM segment and in .impeccable/prints-provenance.txt.
prints.rule: The Graded Print Rule: any raster on a stage is greyscale, blacks lifted to ground, edges burned toward ground with a strength chosen per image, provenance embedded.
prints.window: figure, overflow hidden, background ground; fill + object-fit cover, object-position per project (50% 0). Desktop: right half of the spread, 104px top / 64px bottom, bleeding to the right edge. Mobile: aspect-ratio 4/3 inset by the gutter.

browserSurfaces.scrollbar: width 8px; track var(--bg); thumb var(--line); scrollbar-width: thin

narrative.northStar: La Copia de Cámara Oscura (The Darkroom Print)
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "La Copia de Cámara Oscura" (The Darkroom Print)**

The site is a print pulled from a darkroom, not a web page with a photo on it. One person, one word, and everything else is darkness and grain. The photograph is the argument; the name is the caption. There is no color anywhere: the whole world lives between a near-black ground and a warm paper white, with a single grey for anything that speaks second and a hairline that is barely lighter than the ground. Depth comes from the photograph's own burned edges and a generated silver-gelatin grain, never from CSS gradients, glass, or shadows.

Density is extremely low and deliberate. A stage is a single viewport with a handful of elements, each anchored to an edge or a gutter, and large areas of ground left empty on purpose. Type does the work of hierarchy: a condensed heavy display face at poster scale against small, widely tracked monospace annotations. Body text in Archivo is loaded and reserved but has not yet appeared on a surface; the three shipped stages (Hero, Build, Ship) are entirely display and mono.

Motion is either a print developing or the visitor's own scroll. On load the Hero print "develops" once (1.6s, exponential ease-out) from near-black to its true tones while the caption settles into place. From the second stage on, the page is a sequence of pinned viewports scrubbed by scroll: the Hero's print sinks back into the ground as it leaves, each change of print inside the Build spread is the same 1.6s develop again, and the Ship strip is dragged right-to-left by the scroll while its axis draws once (1.2s, exponential ease-out) on entry. Nothing moves on its own; every motion is tied to load, scroll position, or a hover. The resting state is complete without JavaScript and is shown immediately under `prefers-reduced-motion`, which removes smoothing, pinning and the develop. The product commits to six stages, one word each (Hero, Build, Ship, Prove, Live, Talk); every later stage inherits this world rather than opening a new one.
keyCharacteristics: Black and white only; no color accent exists in the token set.
One dark ground, one ink, one grey, one hairline; nothing in between.
Poster-scale condensed display word against 12–13px tracked monospace annotations.
Flat: no shadows, no CSS vignette on desktop, no radius; edges are the composition.
Generated grain over the whole stage (`mix-blend-mode: overlay`, opacity 0.14).
Every raster is a graded print: greyscale, blacks lifted to ground, edges burned to ground in the asset.
Motion is the develop (1.6s) or the scroll; nothing animates on its own.

rules.name: The No-Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no fifth colour. Emphasis is produced by scale (display vs mono), by value (ink vs mute), or by state (mute → pure white), never by hue.

rules.name: The Burned-In Rule
rules.body: Darkness belongs to the raster. Grading, vignette and the desktop left-field fade live in the image; CSS carries no gradient on desktop. The one CSS fade (the mobile foot veil, `linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 55%, ground 100%)`) exists only where the portrait crop must land on solid ground.

rules.name: The Graded Print Rule
rules.body: Any raster placed on a stage is a print, not a screenshot: converted to greyscale, blacks lifted to `{colors.ground}` so the image never goes darker than the page, and its edges burned toward `{colors.ground}` with a strength chosen per image (heavier on dark sources, lighter on light ones, no burn on an edge that would swallow a white bar), with the grading recipe embedded in the file's own metadata. Colour or an unburned raster never ships.

rules.name: The One Word Rule
rules.body: Each stage owns exactly one display-scale word; everything else on the stage is 12–13px monospace. A stage with two display-scale elements has broken the world.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-Control Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with 0.14em tracking is the voice of bracketed navigation and action links (`[ Build ]`, `[ Talk ]`, `[ Visit raffero.com ]`) only. Descriptor, index and data lines stay in sentence case at 0.06–0.08em, even when they are typed in brackets on mobile.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: No `box-shadow`, no `backdrop-filter`, no glass, no elevation states. If an element needs separation, it gets a 1px hairline (`{colors.line}`) or more empty ground, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Grain Is Material Rule
rules.body: The grain is one static field over the whole stage, regenerated only on resize. Every stage mounts its own Grain canvas at the same opacity and blend; it is never animated, never tiled per element, and never applied to text alone.

rules.name: The Two Pins Rule
rules.body: A pinned stage is scrubbed either by steps (Build: pin length `innerHeight × steps`, active step = `floor(progress × steps)`) or by distance (Ship: pin length `distance × 1.2`, track translated by that distance). Both start `top top`, both `scrub: true`, both vanish at 720px and under `prefers-reduced-motion`, where the stage becomes an ordinary flowing section. A third pin grammar needs a reason these two cannot serve.

dos: Do keep every stage to one display-scale word in Anton (`clamp(96px, 13vw, 200px)`, stepping to `clamp(84px, 24vw, 110px)` at 720px and below) and 12–13px JetBrains Mono for everything else.
Do anchor elements to edges and the gutter (`clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px)`); leave the rest of the stage as ground.

Do use `{colors.mute}` for every secondary voice and `{colors.line}` for every 1px rule (the one exception: a tick that crosses a line-coloured axis is 1px `{colors.mute}`); use pure white only as a hover state.

Do put darkness into the raster (greyscale, blacks lifted to `#0b0b0b`, edges burned toward it in the asset, recipe embedded) and keep the grain canvas over the whole stage at opacity 0.14 with `overlay` blending.
Do ship the resting state complete without JavaScript, and disable smoothing, pinning, the hero exit and the develop under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do type controls as bracketed text (`[ Word ]`) with a 200ms colour step on hover and the global 1px ink focus outline; mark the active item by stepping it to ink, nothing else.

Do reuse the develop (1.6s, `brightness(0.05) contrast(1.6)` → true tones, `--ease-out`) for any print that changes on a stage, and drive stage progress from scroll position (pin + scrub, by steps or by distance) rather than from timers.
Do keep any hairline rectangle transparent and around data only (a Ship frame), and collapse it to hairline-separated rows on mobile and under reduced motion; never box a control.
donts: Don't introduce any hue: no accent colour, no tinted greys, no coloured links or focus rings.
Don't use `box-shadow`, `backdrop-filter`, glass, or CSS gradients on desktop; the only permitted gradient is the mobile foot veil and the 1px scroll cue.
Don't round any corner or draw any box around a control.
Don't cover the finger-on-lips gesture with text at any breakpoint.
Don't uppercase anything except bracketed navigation and action links, and never track the descriptor beyond 0.08em.
Don't animate anything on its own after load; motion is the develop, the scroll-scrubbed pin and hero exit, the once-only axis draw on entry, or the 200ms hover colour step. The grain never moves.
Don't place a colour screenshot, an unburned raster, or a raster without its provenance on a stage.
